title: Protocol for the synthesis of N-Alkyl bromomaleimide linkers
author: Mhlongo, Sharma, et al.

steps.title: Dissolve amine in acetic acid
steps.instruction: Place the respective amine (1.5 mmol) in a round‑bottom flask, add 25 mL glacial acetic acid, and stir on a hot plate until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Add bromomaleic anhydride and reflux
steps.instruction: Add bromomaleic anhydride dropwise (1.5 mmol for compounds 1–4; 3.0 mmol for compound 5) to the stirred solution and reflux.

substeps.instruction: Reflux for 8 h as described in the general protocol (or 3 h as reported in the validation for the same compounds).
For compound 5, use 2 equivalents of bromomaleic anhydride (2 × 1 eq) with ethylenediamine (1 eq) and follow the same reflux conditions.

steps.title: Add acetic anhydride and second reflux
steps.instruction: Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature, add acetic anhydride (2 mL), and reflux the mixture for a further 2 h.

steps.title: Remove solvent under reduced pressure
steps.instruction: Remove acetic acid (and any other volatiles) using a rotary evaporator under reduced pressure.

steps.title: Silica gel column purification
steps.instruction: Purify the crude residue by silica‑gel column chromatography using a mixture of ethyl acetate and n‑hexane as the mobile phase.

substeps.instruction: For butyl amine, elute with 25 % ethyl acetate in n‑hexane.
For dodecyl amine, elute with 1 % ethyl acetate in n‑hexane.
For hexanoic acid, elute with 14 % ethyl acetate in n‑hexane.
For decanoic acid, elute with 5 % ethyl acetate in n‑hexane.
For ethylenediamine, elute with 3 % ethyl acetate in n‑hexane.

steps.title: Collect and concentrate product fractions
steps.instruction: Collect fractions until TLC shows no corresponding spot, then concentrate the combined fractions under reduced pressure on the rotary evaporator.

steps.title: Literature comparison (optional)
steps.instruction: In the reported literature the reaction was heated to 140 °C for longer periods, the crude was washed with toluene, and then purified by silica gel chromatography.
